tasks.title: Bind the delivered exec-upgrade baseline
tasks.objective: Record the already delivered persistent-daemon exec-in-place continuity as the clean baseline for the remaining local Runtime embedding work.
tasks.outcome: The next tasks build on one committed, gated baseline that preserves live Run ownership, replay, and recoverable-Input retry truth across an intentional upgrade.
acceptance: Commit e88bdc5 is reachable from the current tree and contains the bounded handoff manifest, request drain, owner transfer, re-adoption, retry-ledger continuity, and public lifecycle evidence.
The complete repository gate passes from a clean e88bdc5 tree without weakening the checked-in reliability, coverage, fixture, or CI reachability policy.
Cold restart, intentional exec upgrade, Provider-specific resume, and future remote execution remain distinct ownership classes in architecture and protocol truth.

verification.proves: The delivered exec-upgrade baseline and complete repository contract pass from a clean commit.
The exact upgrade ownership, rollback, fail-stop, and non-goal boundary is durable.

tasks.title: Make Integration and Level B ownership explicit
tasks.objective: Finish the public Provider-neutral Integration contract and Level B materialization boundary without moving Provider session or orchestration policy into ctxmux.
tasks.outcome: Embedding clients can detect and register explicit Integrations, materialize an exact Level B Run plan, and receive fail-closed capability results through public SDK surfaces.
acceptance: Integration remains an explicitly imported and registered host-process extension axis, separate from Backend execution location and daemon foundational types.
Level B requires Integration-provided workspace, artifact, lineage, and native-session fidelity and fails explicitly when materialization or provenance is unavailable; no Level A fallback occurs.
Provider-specific session discovery, semantic resume, permissions, prompt parsing, orchestration, and evaluation remain embedding-client responsibilities.
A clean TypeScript consumer proves a valid Level B path and missing-capability, wrong-source, and unavailable-Integration negative space through public APIs.

verification.proves: Integration registration, public Level B behavior, negative space, generated declarations, and repository regressions pass.
Integration, Backend, Runtime, and embedding-client ownership are explicit.

tasks.title: Expose Runtime identity and capability manifest
tasks.objective: Give clients one Provider-neutral description of the compatible Runtime endpoint and the capabilities it can honestly activate or execute.
tasks.outcome: A client can distinguish Runtime identity, protocol compatibility, Backend capabilities, and optional local services without probing private implementation details.
acceptance: Runtime identity is distinct from daemon incarnation, Run identity, Provider identity, build identity, host identity, and remote credentials.
The manifest reports versioned public protocol compatibility and independently declared capabilities; unsupported requests fail explicitly and do not infer behavior from platform or executable names.
The Rust and TypeScript clients consume the same protocol source of truth and the CLI remains a client of that public boundary.
No plugin discovery, marketplace, embedded runtime, transport negotiation framework, or Provider catalog is introduced.

verification.proves: Manifest schema, cross-language parity, compatibility failures, capability negatives, and public clients pass.
Runtime identity and capability semantics have one public protocol owner.

tasks.title: Add revisioned Run observation metadata
tasks.objective: Make Run snapshots and observations orderable without asking clients to infer freshness from receipt arrival or wall-clock polling.
tasks.outcome: Public Run metadata carries one owner-issued revision and well-defined lifecycle timestamps that Rust and TypeScript observers can compare safely.
acceptance: Run revision is monotonic for one Run and changes exactly with publicly observable metadata; clients do not use local receipt order as a substitute.

Creation, start, terminal, interruption, and latest observation timestamps use documented clocks and nullability, survive persistence where claimed, and do not pretend to provide distributed causal time.
Snapshot, attach, event, list, status, fork, cold recovery, and exec-upgrade paths agree on revision and timestamp truth.
Protocol generation, generated TypeScript declarations, SDK validation, persistence schema, CLI presentation, and wrong-case fixtures move together with no compatibility fallback.

verification.proves: Revision monotonicity, timestamp lifecycle, persistence, upgrade, Rust/TypeScript parity, and full regressions pass.
Revision and timestamp meaning, ordering, persistence, and limitations are public.

tasks.title: Provide bounded Rust and TypeScript wait helpers
tasks.objective: Provide one public, deadline-bounded way to wait for Run predicates and terminal state without open-coded polling races across clients.
tasks.outcome: Rust, TypeScript, and CLI consumers share explicit wait semantics over revisioned observations, reconnect, gaps, and terminal outcomes.
acceptance: Rust and TypeScript helpers accept explicit predicates or terminal waits, absolute or duration deadlines, cancellation, and typed timeout, disappearance, transport, and protocol outcomes.
Wait uses public status, attach, event, gap, and reconnect behavior without busy loops, hidden daemon state, unbounded retries, or semantic Agent-status inference.
The CLI wait command reuses the Rust client helper instead of maintaining a second lifecycle algorithm.
Real process tests cover already-satisfied, later-satisfied, exit, interruption, reconnect, gap, cancellation, timeout, daemon replacement, and concurrent waiters.

verification.proves: Rust, TypeScript, CLI, lifecycle, deadline, reconnect, and clean-consumer wait behavior pass.

tasks.title: Provide race-safe TypeScript Runtime activation
tasks.objective: Expose a framework-neutral TypeScript helper that connects to or activates one compatible local ctxmux Runtime while the daemon remains the Run owner.
tasks.outcome: An embedding product can activate, prove readiness, exit, and later reconnect without private spawning logic or coupling daemon life to Node.
acceptance: Concurrent activators converge on one compatible Runtime or return a typed conflict using public identity and readiness, not fixed sleeps.
Live, stale, ordinary-file, symlink, permission, timeout, crashed-launcher, and incompatible-Runtime cases never kill or replace an unrelated target.

The helper exposes explicit executable, socket, state, environment, deadline, and child-disposition inputs and performs no download, global mutation, credential handling, Electron coupling, or SSH fallback.
The activating Node process may exit while daemon-owned Runs survive and a fresh clean consumer reconnects to the same Run and replay.

verification.proves: Activation races, socket safety, readiness, compatibility, caller-exit survival, and SDK regressions pass.
Activation inputs, lifecycle, errors, security boundary, and non-goals are consumer-visible.

tasks.title: Qualify the standalone Runtime embedding surface
tasks.objective: Prove the complete Phase 1 embedding contract from clean external consumers and supported local environments before downstream products consume it.
tasks.outcome: Integration, Level B, Runtime identity, observation metadata, wait, and activation ship as one independently installable public surface with an owner receipt.
acceptance: Fresh Rust and TypeScript consumers install only declared public artifacts and exercise identity, capability, start, observe, wait, activation, Level B, attach, reconnect, stop, and unsupported behavior without repository-private imports.

Clean-environment gates bind exact source, package and binary contents, supported platforms, process survival, filesystem permissions, compatibility, and no hidden ambient daemon or global configuration.
Independent review covers Runtime versus Integration versus Backend versus embedding-product ownership and closes every P0/P1 finding with executable evidence.
The complete repository, coverage, reliability, package, and standalone-consumer gates pass from one clean committed candidate; no package publish, Git push, or hosted release occurs.

verification.proves: The complete repository surface passes on the clean Phase 1 candidate.
Standalone consumer, platform, package, security, lifecycle, and release qualification pass together.
Public claims, evidence, review findings, supported environments, and residual limits are auditable.
